blocks.text: Chapter 21 narrates events during the period conventionally designated as the reigns of Manasseh through Josiah, placing this account within the later monarchic period of Judah. The chapter's position within 2 Kings marks a critical moment in the larger narrative of the kingdom's religious trajectory and its relationship to the covenant.

sections.title: Evaluating Rulers Through Covenant and Prophecy

blocks.text: The book of 2 Kings assesses rulers according to their covenant fidelity and response to the prophetic word. In this framework, political longevity and apparent stability do not constitute success; rather, they are evaluated against standards of obedience to the covenant made with David and Israel. Chapter 21 follows this pattern: it narrates a ruler's religious practices and then presents a prophetic judgment declaring divine response to those practices. For readers of Kings, this evaluative lens remains constant regardless of political circumstances.
